newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower, further slide seen.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower, further slide seen.

text.p: Stocks closed lower on Thursday after a day of narrow fluctuations as jitters over the market's future direction reemerged to haunt the market, brokers said.
"The market seems to be heading for another new year low. Thin trading volume bodes ill for the rest of the month," said Koh Kyong-bae, a broker at Hyundai Securities.
The composite stock index closed 4.29 points lower at a provisional 743.03. It moved between 743.02 and 749.49.
Volume was low with 21.13 million shares changing hands, compared with 23.19 million on Wednesday.
Losers outpaced gainers 433 to 410 with 153 unchanged.

Brokers said the government's announcement that it was against the construction of a new integrated steel mill would dampen sentiment further tomorrow. integrated steel mill capable of producing six million tonnes of crude steel annually."Shares of Hyundai companies and some blue chips are expected to be affected," said Choo Hee-yup, a broker at Dongwon Securities.
Brokers said the appearance this morning of ex-president Choi Kyu-hah in the appeals trial of his successors Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo had little affect on the market.
An overhang of loans for margin trading, and a gloomy economic outlook and an oversupply of stocks were still heavily weighing on the market.
Loans investors owed to securities houses for margin trading were estimated at 2.8 trillion won, compared with 2.6 trillion in customer deposits, brokers said.
But the Japanese yen's appreciation against the dollar and the view that the stock market had bottomed out earlier this week would limit any sharp falls in the index, they said.
